raw_response:
I'm 40 years old, been farming these 600 mu in Quzhou for 20 years since I finished middle school. My farm is big — with just my wife, our kid, and me, there's no way we work it all ourselves. I own a tractor, a combine, and a no-till corn planter, and I hire people whenever there's heavy work.

It's April now. The wheat I planted last October on 420 mu is looking pretty good. I put down base fertilizer before planting — about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. Now at jointing, I'll spread urea, roughly 10 kg of N per mu. I irrigate three times for wheat: green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Pumping water costs money, but I learned two years ago when I skipped one irrigation that losing 80 kg per mu of yield hurts worse than the electricity bill.

My main system is wheat-maize on those same 420 mu. The window between wheat harvest and maize planting is murder — sometimes five days, sometimes three. I plant hybrid maize with my no-till planter the day after the combine finishes. I put down compound fertilizer with the seed, then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage. Total N around 17 kg per mu. Maize usually gives me good money if the weather holds. I irrigate twice — if it rains enough in July, maybe only once.

I keep 120 mu in cotton. Cotton is different — it breaks the grain rotation and the lint prices have been steady. I plant hybrid cotton in late April. The bollworms are the headache, so I spray insecticide four or five times and use herbicide once. N fertilizer about 15 kg per mu, split between planting and flowering. Picking is all hired hands — 15 to 20 people for two rounds in September and October.

The other 60 mu is stevia. I started this because a processing company in the county signs contracts. It's picky — needs more potassium and three irrigations. I transplant seedlings in May and cut twice, July and October. The seedling cost is high but the contract price makes up for it.

I'm not one of those farmers who calculates everything to the last yuan. The extension guy says 15 kg N per mu for wheat, but I usually do closer to 18 because my soil is a bit sandy and I'd rather waste a little fertilizer than lose yield. Last year I tried saving money on cotton pesticide and the worms ate me alive. This year I'm putting in what the crop needs. Total input costs will run about 468,000 yuan, but that's what it takes to run 600 mu properly.
